sentences.text: The genus name Abrosaurus translates to 'delicate lizard' in Greek.
This small sauropod possessed a boxy head featuring a tall bony arch over the nostrils, with large openings separated by thin struts that gave the animal its name.
Reaching a maximum length of 9.1 meters, it stood about 3 meters tall and weighed roughly 10 tons.
Paleontologist Ouyang Hui first described the fossil in a 1986 doctoral thesis before formally naming the species in 1989.
The holotype, a nearly complete skull designated ZDM 5038, comes from the Dashanpu Quarry near Zigong, China.
Today, the holotype skull and other known fossils of Abrosaurus are kept in a museum in Zigong.
Although originally placed among camarasaurids, current research suggests it is a basal member of Macronaria.
The Paleobiology Database lists its parent group as Mamenchisauridae.
Abrosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic Period, approximately 168 to 161 million years ago.
However, the Paleobiology Database records a broader time range from 170.9 to 154.8 million years ago.
The exact placement of Abrosaurus in the sauropod family tree remains difficult to determine because its remains have not been fully described.
